questions.prompt: A flight agent ends a trial with "Your flight has been booked". In Anthropic's terms, what is the outcome?

options.text: Whether a reservation exists in the environment's database.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic defines the outcome as the final state in the environment, not what the agent says.

options.text: The agent's final message to the user at the end of the run.
options.explanation: That message is part of the transcript. The agent can say it booked a flight when no booking exists.

options.text: The number of tool calls the agent made during the trial.
options.explanation: That is a transcript metric you can track. It doesn't tell you whether the task was done.

questions.prompt: You need more test cases for a leasing assistant. What does the OpenAI Cookbook recommend over "generate 50 examples"?

options.text: Copy the same 10 real cases five times to reach 50 cases.
options.explanation: Copies add no new coverage. They only make the same cases count more.

options.text: Ask for 500 examples instead of 50, so the set is bigger.
options.explanation: A bigger request has the same problem: the Cookbook says this often gives a homogenous set.

options.text: List dimensions such as channel, intent and persona, then combine them.
options.explanation: Right. Combining dimensions into tuples gives more diverse, realistic cases. Perturbations such as typos make them harder.

options.text: Only use cases the assistant already passes, to keep results clean.
options.explanation: Then the set can't show any failure. Anthropic says tasks drawn from real failures are a great start.

questions.prompt: Which success criterion fits the Claude docs' advice best?

options.text: The model should give safe outputs when users ask for help.
options.explanation: The Claude docs use "Safe outputs" as their example of a bad criterion: it is not specific or measurable.

options.text: Less than 0.1% of 10,000 outputs flagged for toxicity by a filter.
options.explanation: Right. This is the docs' good example: specific, measurable, and checkable by a test.

options.text: The team feels the outputs are safe after a demo to staff.
options.explanation: OpenAI calls this vibe-based evaluation, an anti-pattern.
